# Observability config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/observability/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.ObservabilityBlock` — the reloadable residue relocated from the kernel broker block: the `log_*` family (level, format, rotation) and, since ADR-122 D5, `dynamic_port_range`. A singleton kind: one `observability` block; the node-id/ops-listen/config-api kernel knobs stay in bootstrap HCL.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `config/observability` |
| Regime | persisted |
| Identity regime | `singleton` — the kind itself is the identity; neither the stem nor a label carries meaning (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| HCL block | `observability` |

| Served at | `GET /api/v1/schemas/config/observability/reference` |

## Example

A minimal `observability`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/observability/example-observability.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

observability {
  log_level = "info"
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `log_level` | string | no | `info` | — | — | Minimum level of the daemon's structured log: "debug" \| "info" \| "warn" \| "error". Hot-reloads without rebuilding the log pipeline. |
| `log_format` | string | no | `text` | — | — | Encoding of each log record: "text" (slog key=value) \| "json" (one object per line). |
| `log_output` | string | no | `stdout` | — | — | Where the daemon writes its structured log: "stdout" \| "stderr" \| "file" \| a file path. "file" is the golden path for a rotated log: it writes <data-dir>/logs/tera.log, under the daemon's --data-dir, with nothing else to choose. Keep "stdout" under systemd or a container runtime, whose journal already rotates it; use "file" under launchd, or anywhere else stdout is redirected to a file nothing rotates. A file destination is always size-bounded and rotated by the log_max_* and log_compress settings, and is opened before it is adopted, so an unwritable one is refused rather than taking the daemon's log dark. While the log is a file, the daemon's Go panics and fatal errors are also written beside it to <log>.crash (a sibling rotation never renames), as well as to its stderr (ADR-023's rotating-writer amendment). |
| `log_max_size_mb` | integer | no | `100` | — | — | Size in megabytes at which a file log_output is rotated: the active file is renamed to a timestamped backup beside it and a fresh one opened. Zero or unset means the default; there is no unbounded setting. Unused when log_output is stdout or stderr. |
| `log_max_age_days` | integer | no | `30` | — | — | Days a rotated backup of a file log_output is kept before it is deleted. Zero or unset means the default: zero is not a spelling of "no limit", and a daemon log has no unbounded retention setting. Unused when log_output is stdout or stderr. |
| `log_max_backups` | integer | no | `5` | — | — | How many rotated backups of a file log_output are kept; older ones are deleted. Zero or unset means the default: zero is not a spelling of "keep every backup", and a daemon log has no unbounded retention setting. Unused when log_output is stdout or stderr. |
| `log_compress` | boolean | no | `true` | — | — | Whether rotated backups of a file log_output are gzip-compressed. Unused when log_output is stdout or stderr. |
| `dynamic_port_range` | string | no | — | — | — | Bounds the ports a listener created after boot may bind, written low-high (e.g. "9100-9199"). Unset means no restriction. Relocated here from the kernel broker block by ADR-122 D5, where it is authored once and reaches the running listener manager on reload; the kernel spelling is retired and refused. |
